newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt issuers rushing to wrap up deals.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt issuers rushing to wrap up deals.

text.p: Corporate debt issuance is expected to come at a brisk pace as issuers struggle to wrap up their financing before the holidays, dealers said.
"We're off to a quiet start but the potential for a busy week is there," said one high-grade syndicate source.
"This is the last full week before the holidays," he observed, adding that if deals "don't get done now they'll get pushed to next year's business."
So far on Monday, Rite Aid Corp's $600 million three-part debt offering is getting set to be launched this afternoon, syndicate sources said.

-Price talk on Rite Aid's $200 million five-year tranche issue is in the 50 to 55 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries. Price talk on the $200 million 10-year issue is seen in the 70 to 75 basis points area.
Price talk on the $200 million 30-year issue is in the 90 to 100 basis points area.
The issues are rated A3/BBB-plus, sources added.
Also, among investment grade issuers, Scholastic Corp is expected to issue $125 million in seven-year notes via Goldman Sachs & Co.
American Re Corp ARN.N is also expected to tap the market with $500 million in 30-year noncallable 144A debt via Goldman Sachs & Co. The deal is expected to be rated Aa1/AA, sources said.

Meanwhile, dealers said with not much left to the calendar year and the Christmas and New Year's holidays approaching the bulk of issuance is likely to be seen this week while desk are still fully staffed.
"As the holiday's approach it becomes difficult to structure these deals as players head out for extended holidays," said another high-grade syndicate source.
"Business is sure to pick up as this is really the last full week to bring deals to market," he added.
Approximately $700 million in new high-yield paper is expected to come to market this week, syndicate sources said.
Among the upcoming high-yield debt offerings are:
- Wilshire Financial Services Group Inc's WFSG.O $75 million in seven-year notes.
- Heartland Wireless Communications Inc's $125 million 144A senior notes due 2004.
- Maxxam Group Holdings' $100 million in 144A notes due 2003 via Bear Stearns & Co.
- TV Filme Inc's $125 million in 144A notes due 2004 via Bear Stearns. Price talk on the issue is in the 12.875 to 13.125 percent area.
- Mechala Group Jamaica Ltd's JAM.N $75 million in three-year 144A notes.
- Lodgenet Entertainment Corp's $125 million in 144A senior unsecured notes due 2006 via Morgan Stanley & Co. Price talk on the issue is in the 10.25 to 10.50 percent area.
- Willcox & Gibbs' $85 million in seven-year 144A notes via Dillon Read & Co.
About $5.5 billion in new straight corporate debt priced in the corporate bond primary market last week, dealers said.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was off 8/32 Monday morning at 98-24/32 to yield 6.60 percent compared with Friday's 6.57 percent at the close.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
